business: BusinessOS (a WhatsApp-native AI assistant that captures a shop's orders and keeps its udhaar book)
by_behaviour: Family-run, son or daughter handles the phone
why_not: Most of my customers just call me, I hardly type anything, and I already have my UPI QR and my diary working. Another thing to learn and keep up every day, no thanks.
Half my orders come by call, and recording every call sounds like extra work I won't keep up with. My paper udhaar diary and UPI QR already work, so I don't see enough reason to change right now.
My diary and my memory already work, and customers who take udhaar are regulars I have known for years. A bot messaging them about money will upset them, and I will not risk that for an app.
Mere customers ka udhaar ka hisaab ek AI ko dene ka mann nahi hai. Maine Khatabook aur OkCredit pehle bhi daala tha, kuch din baad update karna chhod diya; kaagaz ki diary hi chal rahi hai.

Half my orders come by call, so this misses them, and recording every call is a hassle. My stock is in my head and my udhaar is in my diary, and both work fine. I don't see rupees coming back into my till.
Half my orders come by call while I'm serving at the counter, and I can't stop to record each call. So it only covers half my work, and my paper diary already does the udhaar job.
why_yes: I already take most orders on WhatsApp text and voice, and three months free with someone setting it up at my shop costs me nothing to try. I would sign up to test it, but I would only pay the 500 after the free months if it really gets my Hindi right.
flip: If it worked with my phone calls on its own with no extra work from me, and a person in my shop showed me it was right with my own udhaar for a few weeks before I paid anything.
If the person who sets it up stays in my shop for a week, moves my udhaar diary in for me, and I see it catch my phone-call orders without any extra effort from me.
If it picked up my phone-call orders by itself without me recording anything, and the person who sets it up stayed with me for a couple of weeks until it was part of my routine.
If it worked on phone calls on its own without me doing anything, and the person who sets it up stayed and showed me it working with my own customers' udhaar for a week.
If it picked up my phone calls on its own without me recording anything, and the person who visits sets up my existing udhaar diary entries for me, I would try it.

A person from the company sits in my shop for a week and enters my diary into it. I keep the diary running alongside. I can take my full khata out whenever I want, and the price after 3 months stays well under 500.
If my son tried it free on my own real orders for a few weeks and it got them right, and I could see that reminders go out only when I choose, one customer at a time.
If a person I know and trust in my area already uses it for their own shop and shows me that it works, and the khata stays only on my phone and nobody else can see it.
Seeing it work in my own shop for a few weeks, with my diary kept alongside it, and being told the exact price and what happens to my records if I stop paying.
If it worked on its own from my phone calls without me doing anything extra, and the person who sets it up stayed with me until I was comfortable.

A person from the company sits in my shop for a few weeks and runs it alongside my diary, so I can check every entry against the diary. I also need a written promise that I can export my khata and that the price stays fixed after the free months.

Seeing it recover real unpaid udhaar in my own shop within the free months, with the person who sets it up doing the work and entering my old diary for me, and no charge until it has brought in more than 500 rupees.
If it showed me, on my own customers, that it got back more than 500 rupees a month in udhaar I would have forgotten to collect, and it caught phone orders without me recording anything.
If the person who visits sets it up and sits with me for a week, and I see it get my own customers' voice orders right with no extra work from me, I would try the free months.
If it worked on phone calls by itself, with no recording or typing from me, and the person who sets it up stayed until my helpers could use it and my diary matched it for a month.
Seeing it run on my own real orders for a couple of weeks, with a written promise that I pay nothing if it logs wrong orders or I can't show it saved me money.

A person comes to my shop and shows it reading my own real voice notes and my own item names correctly, a day of my actual orders, with no mistakes. Then I would let my son try it free for the 3 months alongside the diary.
If a shopkeeper I know and trust in my own area had been using it for a year, and the diary stayed as my main record while it only copied things down, I would try it for the free months.
If it picked up phone-call orders on its own with no recording, and a person sat with me at the shop for a week showing it gets my udhaar right.
